title: How to build an e-commerce or marketplace app without code
summary: Build a two-sided marketplace, storefront or price comparison app without code. Must-have features, examples and step-by-step tips for each.
body_markdown:
Every great local business starts with someone who sees a better way to connect people with what they need: a baker who wants regulars to preorder Saturday bread, a neighbor who knows half the street can fix bikes or mend clothes, or a deal hunter tired of opening ten tabs. An e-commerce or marketplace app gives you a direct line to buyers, sellers and repeat customers, without paying someone else's commissions or playing by their rules. And you can build one without code.


Building a marketplace or store app without code starts with who it serves and what they need to find, buy or sell. In Thunkable, the AI turns that description into screens and logic. You add login, search and payments, then publish a native app to the App Store and Google Play. This guide walks through the three most common commerce apps, the features each one needs, example apps built with Thunkable, and how to get started.


**In this guide:**


1. Two-sided marketplaces
2. Single-business storefront and ordering apps
3. Price comparison and deal finding apps
4. Feature checklist and FAQ


## **What makes a good commerce app?**


Every successful commerce app answers one question fast: can I find what I want and trust the person selling it? That comes down to three building blocks.


- **Accounts:** Buyers and sellers sign in so orders, messages and history follow them across devices.
- **Discovery:** Search, filters and maps help people find the right item or shop in a few taps.
- **Trust:** Profiles, ratings, messaging and clear checkout reduce the friction that makes people leave.


## **How do you build a two-sided marketplace app?**


A two-sided marketplace app connects people who have something to offer (supply) with people who want it (demand), in a specific niche or region. Think farm-to-buyer produce, local makers, barter and trade, or gig and service work.


**Picture this:** The potter down the street, the family with an overflowing herb garden and the person who mends jeans are all one tap away. Your app becomes the neighborhood market that's open every day.


**Who builds these:** Founders launching a new venture who see an underserved local market or community.


**Inside an example app:** Neighborhood Market, built with Thunkable, is a local marketplace where neighbors sell what they make, grow or fix.


- **Browse:** A feed of listings from your neighborhood, with a search bar (“Find bread, repairs, and more”), category chips for food, services and crafts, and a filter. Listings range from wheel-thrown mugs to herb starts to visible mending, each showing the seller, price and where to meet.
- **Post:** A simple form where anyone can list an offering with a title and description, then publish it to the market.
- **Nearby:** The same listings narrowed to sellers within a couple of miles.


Neighborhood Market app built with Thunkable showing the Browse, listing, Post and Nearby screens.


**Must-have features:**


- **Login and user accounts** so buyers and sellers each have a profile and history
- **Roles** that give buyers, sellers and admins different screens and permissions
- **Cloud sync** so new listings appear for everyone in real time
- **Search and category filters** so buyers find the right item or service fast
- **GPS and maps** to show nearby sellers and meeting spots


**Ways to extend it:** add in-app chat and messaging so buyers can ask questions and arrange pickup without leaving the app, plus ratings to build trust between neighbors.


**Tip:** Marketplaces live or die on early supply. Launch in one neighborhood, like this example's focus on Maplewood, recruit your first sellers by hand, and invite buyers once listings feel full.


## **How do you build a shopping app for your own store?**


A single-business storefront app gives an existing shop or brand its own direct sales channel, so customers buy from you instead of through a third-party platform that takes a commission.


**Picture this:** Your regulars open your app instead of a third-party platform, save their favorites and come back next week. Every sale is yours, and so is the relationship.


**Who builds these:** Boutiques, home goods and gift shops, makers, cafes and local retailers who already have customers and want to keep more of each sale.


**Inside an example app:** This home goods storefront, built with Thunkable, keeps shopping to two tabs.


- **Browse:** A featured “studio pick” up top with price, stock status and shipping time, plus Add to cart and save buttons. Below it, the full catalog of products, each with a photo, price and a short stock note like “Low stock, 3 left” or “4 colors.”
- **Cart:** Everything the customer has added, with a friendly empty state that sends them back to browse.
‍


Home goods store app built with Thunkable showing a featured product, the product catalog and the cart.


**Must-have features:**


- **Product catalog with search and filter** so customers find a product by name, category or price
- **Cart and checkout** connected to a payment provider through API integrations
- **Login** to save addresses, past orders and favorites for faster reordering
- **Cloud sync** so stock levels stay accurate as items sell


**Ways to extend it:** add a **map and store locator** for in-store pickup, **push notifications** for restocks and new arrivals, or **API integrations** with your existing inventory system.


**Tip:** Show stock honestly. Small notes like “3 left” or “Ships in 1 to 2 days,” as this example uses, answer the questions that stop people from buying. Give customers a reason to install, too, like app-only items or a loyalty reward.


## **How do you build a price comparison app?**


A price comparison app gathers prices from several retailers into one place so shoppers can spot the cheapest option without opening a dozen tabs.


**Picture this:** The friend who always knows where to find the best price turns that habit into an app their whole community checks before every big purchase.


**Who builds these:** Deal hunters, niche hobbyists and entrepreneurs who know a category well, such as electronics, groceries, sneakers or fuel.


**Inside an example app:** DealScout, built with Thunkable, starts simple: shoppers enter the prices they find, and the app ranks them.


- **Deals:** A dashboard of saved products and retailers compared, with the best deal for each product front and center and how much it saves versus the highest price. Below it, every retailer's price, ranked lowest to highest.
- **Search:** Find any saved product and revisit the prices collected for it, or add a new one.
- **Saved:** A shortlist of comparisons ready for the next shopping trip, each showing its saved low and a price watch list.
- **You:** How the app works, including which retailers are tracked and that prices are ranked before tax and delivery.


DealScout price comparison app built with Thunkable showing the best deal, price list, Search and Saved screens.


**Must-have features:**


- **Search and filter** to narrow results by product, store or price
- **Cloud sync** so saved comparisons follow the shopper to any device
- **Clear sorting and savings math** that makes the best option obvious at a glance


**Ways to extend it:** add **API integrations** to pull live prices from retailer or affiliate feeds instead of entering them by hand, **charts** to show price history, and **push notifications** for price-drop alerts.


**Tip:** Start manual, then automate. Hand-entered prices, as in this example, let you test whether people want the app before you build data feeds. Be upfront about where prices come from: DealScout tells shoppers prices are entered by hand and to check the retailer before buying.

## **Frequently asked questions**


**Can I build a marketplace app without coding?**


Yes. Thunkable's AI generates screens and logic from a description, and you can add sign-in and connect a free Supabase account for a cloud database. No coding is required to get started.


**What's the difference between a native app and a web app in a wrapper?**


A native app is built for iOS and Android, so it can use device features like the camera, barcode scanning and push notifications directly. A wrapped app is a website inside an app shell, which can feel slower and may lose access to some device features. Thunkable builds native apps, so your store feels like it belongs on your customers' phones.


**What features does a marketplace app need?**


At minimum: user login, separate buyer and seller roles, real-time cloud sync and in-app messaging. Location-based marketplaces also need GPS and maps.


**Is a marketplace or a single-store app easier to launch?**


A single-store app is usually easier, because you already have products and customers. A marketplace has to attract both buyers and sellers at the same time.


**Can I take payments in my app?**


Yes. For digital goods, subscriptions and premium content, Thunkable's in-app purchase blocks connect to RevenueCat and work in iOS and Android apps. For physical products, like orders from your store or marketplace, connect a payment provider such as Stripe through Thunkable's Web API blocks. Apple and Google require their own in-app purchase systems for digital content, so choose the option that matches what you sell.


**Will my app be on the App Store and Google Play?**


Yes. Thunkable builds native iOS and Android apps you can publish to both stores. Store publishing is included on the Builder and Advanced plans.
